findings.evidence: Lines 90–91 use only `Ideal.absNorm_ne_zero_iff_mem_nonZeroDivisors`, `hnorm`, and `q.Prime.ne_zero`; no genus-field or squarefreeness property enters the proof.
findings.fix: Generalize it to an arbitrary ideal over an infinite Dedekind domain with hypotheses `Ideal.absNorm I = n` and `n ≠ 0`, or make this convenience lemma private and inline the existing Mathlib equivalence.
findings.issue: `mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_absNorm_eq_prime` unnecessarily requires a squarefree `d`, the candidate genus-field base, and primality; its proof only needs an ideal norm equal to a nonzero natural.

findings.evidence: Lines 117–129 use only the two zero-sum equalities, finite-sum erasure, cancellation, and agreement away from `P`; no property of prime discriminants, `d`, or `ZMod 2` is used.
findings.fix: State the underlying lemma for functions on an arbitrary finite type into an additive cancellative commutative monoid/group whose sums agree, then specialize it here; alternatively keep this one-off specialization private.
findings.issue: `candidateGenusFieldRelativeSignSubmodule_eq_of_forall_ne` is presented as a reusable parity argument but is restricted to the candidate genus-field index type and `ZMod 2`.

summary: Two newly public helper lemmas are specialized to genus-field objects despite proofs that use only generic ideal-norm or finite-sum structure.
